To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the incidence of gastric cancer after proximal gastric resection for ulcer is not increased, but that there is a significant increase in the incidence of gastric stump carcinoma after truncal vagotomy and gastrojejunostomy.

1) the recurrence rate after proximal gastric (PG) vagotomy with ulcer excision in patients with type I gastric ulcer is 17.5% at 5 years; 2) recurrence rates after proximal gastric and pyloric and pre-pyloric ulcer are significantly higher (35% at 5-years); and 3) recurrence is mainly gastric and can be treated conservatively.
1. Proximal gastric vagotomy with ulcer excision is the treatment of choice for gastric ulcers type I and probably also type II.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the results of proximal gastric vagotomies (PGV) for gastric, pyloroduodenal and duodenal ulcer disease.
the recurrence rate after proximal gastric and combined gastric and duodenulcer after proximal gastric resection.
the results of proximal gastric vagatomy (PGV) for gastric ulcer (GU) and pyloric and pre-pyloric ulcers (PUPU) and the results of reoperations in case of recurrent ulcers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PGV with ulcer removal for gastric ulcer type 1 is the operation of choice.
PGV with ulcer resection is a good operation for gastric ulcer type 1 and probably for gastric ulcer type II.
the operation of choice for gastric ulcer type III is vagotomy and antectomy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PGV with ulcer removal for gastric ulcer type 1 and 2 (according to Johnson), as well as pyloric and pre-pyloric ulcer, is a safe procedure with a recurrence rate similar to that for duodenal ulcera.
the recurrence rate after proximal gastric (PGV) is similar for gastric and duodenul ulcers, but significantly higher for pyloric and prepiloric ulcers.
the recurrence rate of gastric ulcer type I after PGV with excision is low.

the current literature on the use of laparoscopic gastric bypass for weight loss is of poor methodological quality and is characterized by a high risk of bias.
